The\n49\tcorrect reading — and what the code does — is: **all six route through the shared\n50\t`get_formatter()` factory**, and each picks the trait method that matches its data\n51\tshape. The issue-array commands (`list`/`ready`/`search`) use `format_issues()`;\n52\tthe object/array commands use their dedicated methods. This is the intended,\n53\tdocumented design (see the doc-comments on `ClaimResultOutput` and `StatsOutput`).\n54\t\n55\t---\n56\t\n57\t## Per-command results\n58\t\n59\t### `list --format json`\n60\t- **Path:** `cmd_list` → `get_formatter(fmt).format_issues(&issues)`\n61\t- **Output:** JSONL — one full `Issue` object per line.\n62\t- **Fields:** `assignee` always present (`null` when unset), `labels` always an\n63\t  array (`[]` when empty) — the bf-1wj display contract.\n64\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON.\n65\t\n66\t### `ready --format json`\n67\t- **Path:** `cmd_ready` → resolves each scored candidate to its full `Issue` via\n68\t  `storage.get_issue`, then `get_formatter(Json).format_issues(&issues)`. This\n69\t  routing was added in **bf-64zt** (previously it emitted a custom JSON array of\n70\t  `ScoredBead` summaries).\n71\t- **Output:** JSONL, identical shape to `list`.\n72\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON (the last issue-array command to be migrated).\n73\t\n74\t### `search --format json`\n75\t- **Path:** `cmd_search` → `get_formatter(fmt).format_issues(&issues)`\n76\t- **Output:** JSONL, identical shape to `list`.\n77\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON.\n78\t\n79\t### `claim --format json`\n80\t- **Path:** `cmd_claim` → `get_formatter(fmt).format_claim_result(&out)` /\n81\t  `format_no_claim()`.\n82\t- **Output:** a single JSON object — `{\"bead_id\",\"assignee\",\"reclaimed\"}` on a\n83\t  real claim, with `dry_run`/`title`/`priority`/`downstream_impact`/`workspace`\n84\t  added on `--dry-run`. `{}` when nothing is available.\n85\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON.\n86\t\n87\t### `stats --format json`\n88\t- **Path:** `cmd_stats` → `get_formatter(fmt).format_stats(&StatsOutput)`.\n89\t- **Output:** a single JSON object with `total`/`open`/`in_progress`/`closed`,\n90\t  plus `by_type`/`by_priority`/`by_assignee`/`by_label` nested maps **folded in**\n91\t  when requested. Folding (rather than appending text) keeps `stats --by-*`\n92\t  output a single valid JSON document — the bug class fixed when `StatsOutput`\n93\t  was introduced.\n94\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON.\n95\t\n96\t### `velocity --format json`\n97\t- **Path:** `cmd_velocity` → `get_formatter(fmt).format_velocity(&[VelocityStats])`.\n98\t- **Output:** a JSON array (`[]` when there are no claim→close events).\n99\t- ✅ No ad-hoc JSON.\n100\t\n101\t---\n102\t\n103\t## The strongest consistency proof\n104\t\n105\t`issue_array_commands_share_formatter` creates one bead and runs `list`, `ready`,\n106\tand `search` with `--format json`. For that bead, all three emit **byte-identical**\n107\tJSON:\n108\t\n109\t```\n110\tlist   line == ready  line == search line\n111\t```\n112\t\n113\tByte-identity is only possible if all three serialize the same `Issue` through the\n114\tsame `JsonFormatter`. So this test is simultaneously:\n115\t\n116\t- the runtime proof that `list`/`ready`/`search` share the formatter, and\n117\t- the runtime proof that **no custom `println!` JSON loop** survives in any of\n118\t  them (a divergent hand-rolled loop would emit a different field set or order and\n119\t  fail the equality).\n120\t\n121\tThis is reinforced by a static check: a `grep -n serde_json src/cli/mod.rs` shows\n122\t**zero** `serde_json` references inside the six in-scope handlers. Every remaining\n123\t`serde_json` call lives in an out-of-scope command (see below).\n124\t\n125\t---\n126\t\n127\t## Known, deliberate asymmetry: empty results\n128\t\n129\tThe audit found exactly one inconsistency, and it is **intentional**:\n130\t\n131\t| Command | Empty result (`--format json`) |\n132\t|---------|-------------------------------|\n133\t| `list`   | empty stdout (0 bytes) |\n134\t| `search` | empty stdout (0 bytes) |\n135\t| `recent` | empty stdout (0 bytes) |\n136\t| `ready`  | `[]` |\n137\t| `claim`  | `{}` |\n138\t| `stats`  | `{\"total\":0,\"open\":0,\"in_progress\":0,\"closed\":0}` |\n139\t| `velocity` | `[]` |\n140\t\n141\t`list`/`search`/`recent` model their output as **JSONL**: zero lines *is* zero\n142\tbeads, so empty input legitimately produces no output. `ready` prints `[]` instead\n143\t— a contract **deliberately preserved** when bf-64zt migrated `ready` to the shared\n144\tformatter (its commit message: *\"Empty result prints `[]` (preserving the prior\n145\tempty-array contract)\"*). `claim`/`stats`/`velocity` always emit valid JSON objects\n146\tor arrays.\n147\t\n148\t**Decision for this bead:** do not change runtime behavior. The `[]` contract was\n149\tset on purpose by a prior bead, and `tests/ready_json_fields.rs` already tolerates\n150\tit. Changing it risks breaking downstream consumers (e.g. a NEEDLE strand) that\n151\tbf-64zt explicitly protected. The\ncorrect reading — and what the code does — is: **all six route through the shared\n`get_formatter()` factory**, and each picks the trait method that matches its data\nshape. The issue-array commands (`list`/`ready`/`search`) use `format_issues()`;\nthe object/array commands use their dedicated methods.
